seatMission: Verify that material claims and calculations resolve to valid, faithful, traceable sources without becoming a substitute for domain judgment.
seatResponsibilities: Verify that material claims resolve to valid sources and calculations.

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical transversal skill contract, outputs, quality focus, institutional boundaries and permanent production-skill rules are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. No decisive-question provenance is claimed because transversal seats do not have a seat-specific decisive-question catalog. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I identify which factual, quantitative, legal, technical, or causal claims require verifiable support.
I distinguish material claims from common connective language that does not require citation.
I separate one sentence into multiple claims when each requires different support.
I recognize when a recommendation contains embedded factual premises that must be verified.
I identify claims whose consequence demands stronger provenance than ordinary background assertions.
I distinguish externally verifiable claims from internal decisions, values, or preferences.
I flag uncited numbers, dates, thresholds, quotations, and comparative assertions that could affect a decision.
I identify when a claim is actually an inference and requires both source support and explicit inference labeling.
I avoid treating the presence of any citation as proof that every nearby claim is supported.
I define the verification unit precisely enough that citation quality can be judged claim by claim.
I verify that every citation resolves to an identifiable source rather than a dead or ambiguous reference.
I confirm that source identifiers, links, document IDs, pages, sections, or record keys point to the intended material.
I distinguish a source homepage or repository from the precise record supporting a claim.
I detect citations that resolve to a different version, entity, jurisdiction, or document than intended.
I verify that citations remain usable by the authorized reviewers who need to inspect them.
I identify broken, inaccessible, malformed, or nonpersistent citation targets.
I preserve stable identifiers when URLs or display names can change.
I distinguish citation aliases from independent sources so duplicate references do not inflate support.
I verify that machine-readable provenance fields correspond to the human-readable citation.
I treat source resolution as a prerequisite to evaluating whether the source actually supports the claim.
I verify the author, issuer, owner, or system of record when source authority matters.
I distinguish primary sources from secondary commentary, summaries, and copied material.
I identify when several citations ultimately derive from the same upstream source.
I assess whether source jurisdiction, scope, population, period, and purpose fit the claim being supported.
I flag anonymous, unattributed, or unverifiable material when provenance weakness affects reliance.
I distinguish independently produced evidence from vendor, advocacy, or interested-party claims.
I preserve publication, effective, retrieval, and version dates when each has different provenance meaning.
I identify provenance gaps introduced by exports, screenshots, transformations, or copied excerpts.
I verify that internal evidence points back to an authoritative record when one exists.
I report source-authority limitations without substituting my own opinion about the business conclusion.
I verify that a cited source actually supports the specific claim made, not merely the general topic.
I detect claims that are stronger, broader, more certain, or more causal than their sources support.
I distinguish evidence that supports a fact from evidence that supports only an interpretation.
I verify that qualifiers, exceptions, populations, and conditions in the source are preserved in the claim.
I flag citation mismatch when a source supports only part of a compound statement.
I detect when correlation, association, forecast, or expert opinion has been rewritten as established causation.
I verify that negative or null findings have not been cited as positive evidence.
I ensure comparisons preserve the source definitions and baselines required for a valid comparison.
I identify cherry-picked support when nearby source context materially changes the cited meaning.
I calibrate citation-validity findings to what the source can actually entail rather than what the author likely intended.
I verify quoted text against the source and preserve wording accurately within allowed quotation limits.
I distinguish direct quotation from paraphrase and summary.
I check that ellipses, truncation, or excerpt boundaries do not reverse or distort source meaning.
I verify that quoted speakers, authors, dates, and contexts are attributed correctly.
I preserve surrounding conditions when an isolated quotation would be misleading.
I detect quotations copied from secondary sources when the original source is claimed.
I flag translated quotations when the translation materially affects meaning and provenance.
I ensure quotation punctuation or formatting does not create words absent from the source.
I identify stale quotations from superseded policy, contracts, guidance, or versions.
I treat contextual faithfulness as part of citation correctness rather than a stylistic concern.
I verify that material numbers can be traced to source inputs, formulas, transformations, and model versions.
I distinguish observed data from calculated, estimated, forecast, or simulated values.
I confirm units, currencies, denominators, periods, populations, and definitions across a calculation chain.
I identify manual constants or overrides whose provenance is not documented.
I verify that derived metrics can be recomputed from the cited inputs when reproducibility is required.
I trace sensitivity and scenario results to the assumptions that generated them.
I detect when rounded presentation values no longer reconcile with the underlying calculation.
I distinguish a cited data source from a valid calculation based on that data.
I flag spreadsheet, code, or model outputs whose input lineage or version cannot be established.
I require calculation traceability proportionate to the decision consequence of the quantitative claim.
I verify that citations refer to the source version valid for the claim's relevant time.
I distinguish publication date, effective date, observation period, retrieval date, and last-modified date.
I detect citations to sources superseded by newer law, policy, documentation, data, or organizational state.
I preserve historical citations when the claim concerns what was known or true at an earlier decision point.
I flag temporal mismatch when evidence and claim describe incompatible periods.
I avoid declaring a source stale solely because it is old when historical evidence is the relevant evidence.
I verify current-status claims against sufficiently current sources.
I identify citations to mutable web content that lack retrieval or version context.
I detect when a downstream artifact cites a current summary for a historical claim whose earlier version differs.
I make temporal-validity findings explicit so downstream roles can distinguish stale support from wrong support.
I trace derivative summaries, extracts, embeddings, datasets, and artifacts back to their originating sources.
I distinguish direct evidence from transformations that may introduce interpretation or loss.
I verify that provenance survives format conversion, export, aggregation, or redaction.
I identify when a derivative source combines multiple originals and requires multiple lineage links.
I detect circular citation chains in which artifacts cite one another without reaching primary evidence.
I verify that transformed data preserves the source fields needed to justify downstream claims.
I flag provenance breaks caused by copy-paste, screenshots, detached attachments, or undocumented preprocessing.
I preserve transformation metadata when filtering, normalization, or aggregation changes what a source represents.
I distinguish a model-generated statement from the evidence sources used to generate it.
I require derivative lineage to remain inspectable enough for an authorized reviewer to reconstruct the support chain.
I record missing citations separately from citations that resolve but fail to support the claim.
I classify citation defects by type so remediation addresses the actual provenance failure.
I identify when two valid citations support materially contradictory claims rather than declaring one invalid automatically.
I preserve evidence disagreement for the appropriate contradiction or domain role to evaluate.
I flag claims supported only by inaccessible sources when reviewers cannot verify them.
I distinguish source-quality weakness from complete absence of provenance.
I identify claims whose citation gaps block progression because the claim is material to the decision.
I avoid replacing a failed citation with a superficially similar source that does not support the same claim.
I preserve the original defect and remediation trail when a citation is corrected.
I state when no valid source can be found rather than fabricating or stretching provenance.
I report citation validation in a structured form that names the claim, source, result, and defect when present.
I distinguish verified support, partial support, unsupported claims, unresolved access, and contradictory evidence.
I preserve the source and calculation identifiers needed for downstream audit.
I avoid rewriting a domain conclusion merely because its citation is defective.
I send substantive interpretation disputes to the appropriate domain or governance role rather than resolving them by citation authority.
I make clear when citation validity does not imply the source itself is true, complete, or sufficient for the business decision.
I verify citations independently of whether I agree with the recommendation they support.
I preserve dissenting evidence and its valid provenance even when the dominant recommendation differs.
I make remediation requirements specific enough that an artifact can be corrected and rechecked.
I treat citation and provenance checking as assurance of traceability, not as ownership of truth, synthesis, certification, or approval.
